open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-001 verification binding
open_points.text: PLAT-REG-001: a focused test at `validate_project_reference` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to prove that the portal never generates a Registry project_id and refuses a violating input without writes?
options: Bind a check that attempts portal-generated project identity and proves refusal with no writes
Leave PLAT-REG-001 without a witnessing check
open_points.default_guess: Add a focused bound check at `validate_project_reference`.

witness.initial: Registry has no project P and the portal has no records for P.
events: A staff caller submits a linked write naming P.
The implementation handles the unknown identifier.
outcomes: The implementation refuses because only Registry may create project identity and writes nothing.
The implementation creates or adopts P locally and completes the linked write; no bound check named by A5 detects it.
witness.observer: The staff caller and Registry operators

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-002 verification binding
open_points.text: PLAT-REG-002: the ledger's property at `_validate_reference_identity` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to prove that linkage uses the returned UUID rather than display name or address?
options: Bind a property check with colliding display names or addresses and mismatched UUIDs
Leave PLAT-REG-002 without a witnessing check
open_points.default_guess: Bind a property check that exercises a returned UUID mismatch.

witness.initial: Registry projects A and B have the same display name; the requested UUID is A and the response identifies B.
events: A staff actor performs a linked write for A.
The gateway returns B's UUID with the shared display name.
outcomes: UUID-based validation refuses the response and changes nothing.
Name-based validation accepts the response and links the write to the wrong project.
witness.observer: The staff actor and clients of projects A and B

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-006 verification binding
open_points.kind: bound checks do not prove invariant
open_points.text: PLAT-REG-006: a focused test at `get_project_context` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What bound check actually calls the real `get_project_context` boundary and distinguishes a live Registry fetch from cached or persisted Registry context?
options: Bind a check that changes Registry context between reads and requires the new live value
Treat checks that replace the Registry functions with stubs as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Require a focused gateway check that observes two different live Registry answers.

witness.initial: Project P was named Old and active when the portal last read it; Registry now names it New and marks it archived.
events: A viewer opens P after the Registry change.
The portal builds the project context.
outcomes: A live-fetch implementation returns New and archived/read-only.
A cached-snapshot implementation returns Old and active; both supplied bound checks can still pass because they substitute the Registry boundary.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-007 verification binding
open_points.text: PLAT-REG-007: a focused test at `create_viewer` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to prove that viewer display_name remains independent of Registry customer_ref?
options: Bind a create/read check with deliberately different viewer display_name and Registry customer_ref
Leave PLAT-REG-007 without a witnessing check
open_points.default_guess: Bind a focused `create_viewer` check using unequal values.

witness.initial: Registry project P has customer_ref `ACME-42`; an administrator creates viewer V with display_name `Familia García`.
events: The administrator creates V and grants P.
Registry later changes customer_ref to `ACME-99`.
V and the administrator read V's portal identity.
outcomes: The portal continues to show `Familia García`.
The portal derives or synchronizes the viewer name from customer_ref and shows `ACME-42` or `ACME-99`.

open_points.subject: INV-020 snapshot immutability check
open_points.text: INV-020: a focused test at `import_snapshot` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Must the bound check re-read the accepted snapshot after a conflicting republication and prove every field is unchanged, rather than checking only row counts and the conflict result?
options: Require an exact before/after snapshot comparison after the conflict
Treat unchanged snapshot row count as proof of immutability
open_points.default_guess: Require exact re-reading and equality of the original snapshot.

witness.initial: An accepted snapshot S contains approved_by `Alice` and one snapshot row exists.
events: The producer republishes the same identity with approved_by `Bob`.
The import returns `integrity_conflict` and the snapshot row count remains one.
outcomes: The stored snapshot remains byte-for-byte equal to S.
The implementation overwrites the existing row with Bob while returning the conflict; the supplied check's counts and result still pass.
witness.observer: A staff actor later reading or activating the snapshot

open_points.subject: INV-022 producer activation prohibition
open_points.text: INV-022: a focused test at `activate_budget_version` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Must the bound check exercise a service producer attempting activation, in addition to rejecting a staff context with the wrong capability?
options: Test activation with a service actor or producer-derived context and prove no writes
Treat rejection of an ordinary context lacking the activation capability as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit producer-activation refusal case.

witness.initial: Producer S has imported snapshot version V, which is inactive.
events: S invokes activation for V using its authenticated producer identity.
The activation operation evaluates its caller.
outcomes: The operation refuses S and V remains inactive.
An implementation special-cases the importing producer and activates V; the supplied budget check never uses a producer actor and still passes.
witness.observer: The producer, staff reviewers, and client viewers

open_points.subject: INV-023 atomic budget activation
open_points.text: INV-023: a focused test at `activate_budget_version` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What failure case in the bound check proves that deactivating the old version and activating the new version are atomic?
options: Force a failure after one status change and require both original statuses to remain
Infer atomicity from a successful activation that ends with one active version
open_points.default_guess: Add a forced mid-operation or audit failure and assert complete rollback.

witness.initial: Project P has active version A and inactive version B.
events: Staff activates B.
A forced audit or persistence failure occurs after A is deactivated but before B is committed active.
outcomes: The transaction rolls back: A remains active and B inactive.
A remains inactive and B inactive; the supplied successful-activation scenario still passes on an implementation without this rollback guarantee.

open_points.subject: INV-024 imported-plan immutability
open_points.text: INV-024: a focused test at `upsert_manual_section_plan` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: How does the bound check prove that imported plans are immutable copies of their snapshot, rather than only proving manual-budget reuse and archived-project refusal?
options: Attempt to edit an imported plan and require refusal with exact stored values unchanged
Treat manual-plan scenarios as sufficient for the whole invariant
open_points.default_guess: Add an imported-plan edit refusal and snapshot-copy equality check.

witness.initial: Imported inactive version V has a section plan copied from snapshot S with material_planned 100.00.
events: A staff actor submits a plan upsert targeting V with material_planned 250.00.
outcomes: The operation refuses and V remains an exact copy of S.
The operation edits V to 250.00; the supplied check only edits manual plans and still passes.
witness.observer: Staff reviewers and client viewers after activation

open_points.subject: INV-025 section linking
open_points.kind: bound check does not exercise owner
open_points.text: INV-025: a focused test at `_link_snapshot_sections` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What bound scenario calls `_link_snapshot_sections` with equal names but unequal source_key values and proves that only source_key equality links sections?
options: Bind a direct linking check covering equal keys, unequal keys, and equal display names
Treat activation scenarios that never call `_link_snapshot_sections` as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add the direct source-key-versus-display-name linking check.

witness.initial: Existing section E has source_key `kitchen-v1` and display name `Kitchen`; a new snapshot section N has source_key `kitchen-v2` and the same display name.
events: The imported version's sections are linked.
outcomes: N creates a new PortalSection because the source keys differ.
N is linked to E by display name; the supplied budget check never invokes `_link_snapshot_sections` and still passes.
witness.observer: An operator resolving allocations and clients viewing section history

open_points.subject: INV-026 planned-budget independence
open_points.text: INV-026: a focused test at `import_snapshot` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to prove that later expense or mutable producer-state changes cannot alter planned budget values?
options: Bind a history that changes expenses and producer state after import and proves the stored/visible plan is unchanged
Leave INV-026 without a witnessing check

witness.initial: Snapshot S establishes planned materials of 500.00 and the project has an expense of 100.00.
events: S is imported.
The expense is corrected to 200.00 and the producer's mutable estimate changes to 700.00.
Staff reads the portal budget.
outcomes: Planned materials remain 500.00.
An implementation recomputes planned materials from the expense or live producer state and reports 200.00 or 700.00.

open_points.subject: INV-027 derived aggregates
open_points.text: INV-027: a focused test at `build_budget_view` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to prove that financial aggregates are never stored as editable state and are recomputed after owning records change?
options: Bind a check that changes an owning record and requires the next view to recompute the total
Leave INV-027 without a witnessing check

witness.initial: The active plan is 500.00 and included allocations total 100.00; a first view reports those totals.
events: An operator replaces allocations so the included total becomes 200.00.
The client reads the budget again.
outcomes: The second view recomputes and reports 200.00 actual.
The implementation returns an editable or stale stored aggregate of 100.00; a one-shot view test can still pass.

open_points.subject: INV-028 referenced-section deletion
open_points.text: INV-028: a focused test at `PortalTransaction.commit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to attempt deletion of a PortalSection referenced by an allocation or progress record and prove complete refusal?
options: Bind a commit-level deletion attempt with allocation and progress references
Leave INV-028 without a witnessing check
open_points.default_guess: Bind a commit-level foreign-reference preservation test.

witness.initial: Section S is referenced by expense allocation A and progress record G.
events: A transaction attempts to delete S and commits.
outcomes: Commit is refused and S, A, and G remain unchanged.
Commit deletes S, either orphaning or cascading A and G; no check bound by A18 detects it.
witness.observer: Operators and clients reading expenses and progress

open_points.subject: INV-033 replacement-allocation witness
open_points.text: Witness: `replace_expense_allocations` with the explicit amounts 150.00 to a section and 50.00 to other expenses persists exactly those two allocations, and a replacement of 1.00 against the 200.00 total is refused with `ExpenseValidationError` while the stored row counts stay unchanged; nothing spreads an amount (`verification/client_portal_expense_consumer_support.py`, run by the check) [witness: verification:expense_management_uow_client_portal].
open_points.question: Does the bound check actually execute assertions for exact 150.00/50.00 persistence and unchanged stored rows after the mismatched 1.00 replacement, given that the supplied check only delegates to an unprovided helper?
options: Provide or bind check content containing those exact value and no-write assertions
Accept the delegating wrapper and prose claim without inspectable assertions
open_points.default_guess: Require the helper content or an equivalent directly inspectable focused check.

witness.initial: Expense E totals 200.00 and currently has valid allocations.
events: An operator replaces allocations with explicit 150.00 to section S and 50.00 to other expenses.
The operator then attempts a replacement containing only 1.00.
The verification wrapper runs `run_management_checks`.
outcomes: A conforming implementation stores exactly 150.00 and 50.00, then refuses 1.00 with no row changes.

An implementation spreads the first request as 100.00/100.00 but still creates distinct allocation ids and refuses the 1.00 mismatch; the visible wrapper passes if the unavailable helper checks only distinct ids and sum refusal.
witness.observer: The verification gate and clients viewing allocation amounts

open_points.subject: INV-050 deterministic derivation
open_points.text: INV-050: a focused test at `build_project_overview` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to run the same accepted records through `build_project_overview` repeatedly and prove equality of every derived component?
options: Bind a repeated-read determinism check with deliberately ambiguous repository order
Leave INV-050 without a witnessing check

witness.initial: A project has two expenses and two payments with equal primary dates, while repository iteration order can vary.
events: A client reads the overview twice without any intervening state change.
The repository returns the equal-date records in opposite raw orders.
outcomes: Both overview answers are identical because derivation and ordering are deterministic.
The answers differ in list order or a dependent aggregate; no check is bound to INV-050.

open_points.subject: INV-052 append-only audit and import records
open_points.text: INV-052: a focused test at `PortalTransaction.commit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Where does the bound check attempt to update or delete an existing AuditRecord and SnapshotImportRecord and prove commit refuses both without any change?
options: Add commit-level update and delete attempts for both record types
Treat duplicate-insert and rollback scenarios as proof of append-only storage
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit mutation and deletion refusal cases.

witness.initial: Import record I and audit record A have been committed.
events: A later transaction changes I's outcome and deletes A, then commits.
outcomes: Commit is refused and both records remain exactly unchanged.
The transaction succeeds because storage exposes update/delete paths; the supplied snapshot check, which exercises inserts, duplicates, and rollbacks, still passes.
witness.observer: The producer reading I and an auditor reading A
